To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thrombospondin‐induced apoptosis is mediated by TNF receptors in primary human brain microvascular endothelium.
thrombospondin‐induced apoptosis is mediated by tumor necrosis factor‐R1.
thrombospondin‐induced apoptosis in brain microvascular endothelium requires TNF‐α and TNF‐R.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new anti‐angiogenic factors that may be useful in the treatment of cancer.
the role of the extracellular matrix in angiogenesis.
the role that thrombospondin‐2 (TSP‐2) plays in the regulation of the angiogenic response to vascular injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TSP‐ 1 induces apoptosis in primary human brain MVEC, which is mediated, in part, by TNF‐α and its receptor, TNF‐R 1.
TSP1 induced apoptosis in brain microvascular endothelium through a mechanism involving TNFR1 and caspase-8 and that the TSP1-induced TNF-α was required for the induction of apoptosis.
thrombospondin‐ 1‐induced endothelial apoptosis in the brain can be mediated by tumor necrosis factor‐1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TSP‐I induced apoptosis of primary human brain microvascular endothelium (HBMEC) is mediated by the TNF‐R pathway.

TSP‐induced endothelial apoptosis is mediated by TNFα, which in turn, requires TNFα receptor 1 (TNRα1), and that TSP1‐induced endothelium apoptosis can be reversed by TSP2, which can bind to the same receptor as TSP1, and thus, can act as an anti‐angiogenic agent.
TSP-1 induces apoptosis of brain microvessel endothelial cells through TNF-R1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thrombospondin‐induced endothelial cell apoptosis can occur by a mechanism that is mediated by TNFα and the TNF receptor‐1.
thrombospondin‐induced cell death is mediated by TNFα.
the thrombospondin‐induced apoptosis is mediated by TNF receptors.
